notes.title: Qyllscape Update V 1.0.6
notes.content:
Hello!

I am back to share that update v1.0.6 is live! Just a note, if you ever have issues with an update, I am now creating beta branches for the previous versions, so in Steam if you right-click on Qyllscape, go to properties, and then Betas, you can choose to roll back your version if you would like.

Below I'll list some of the updates, but I have added information to the official manual (Found [url=https://www.qyllscape.com/support.html]here[/url]), so make sure to look over that as well if you have any questions.

[h2]Settings Quick Search[/h2]

Probably my favorite part of this update, use [b]ctrl + /[/b] to bring up a settings quick search dialog which will allow you to summon the appropriate settings panel based on keywords.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/adf101a6080599bf28a4d908bf888f3436bf2da9.png[/img]

I have found this to be way faster than pressing 'escape' and navigating the menus, so I'm excited to share it, and hope you find it helpful as well.

[h2]User Uploaded Content[/h2]

There is now the ability to upload your own background images and fonts, using the corresponding dialogs. Once you drag and drop either a [b].png[/b] file for backgrounds, or a [b].ttf[/b] file for fonts, you will see them in the dropdown list within the panel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/baa7e244dc87637e3b69eb42cc6a669ab1c68b26.png[/img]

Please note that I've tested this on my own machines, but it still qualifies as an experiment and dragging in files could potentially cause unexpected issues, but at any time you can delete the created [b]textures[/b] or [b]fonts[/b] folders to get rid of the added options.

[h2]Font and Details[/h2]

Aside from uploading fonts, it is also important to mention that the font and page detail settings have been moved to their own panel. Along with this is the added ability to specify custom text for the left and right page titles. This will allow you to add whatever you want, just as I've opted to add my name as the author in the example below, while the left page title is defaulting to the project name.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/af362223a214c57bd25a2a03e4349b699da244af.png[/img]

[h2]Rich Text Workaround[/h2]

I have found a temporary (not perfect) solution for rich text formatting within the framework Qyllscape is built on. Using shortcuts like ctrl + i, ctrl + b, and ctrl + u will now add css tags to selected text. You will unfortunately not see these effects within Qyllscape, but they will appear in your exported HTML file, which is easily converted to PDF within a browser.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/b70e1f2239e0822ef94acb4e588ff6dc0315938a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/fe71284f6dd19d9078183adeb9540b7600bb8529.png[/img]

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]

That's a few cool things for version 1.0.6. Please continue to let me know if you encounter any big issues, and I hope you enjoy this small update. I am continuing to think about improvements and experiment as I go along, so thank you for being patient. Soon I will start thinking about pushing for a version 1.1 which may include some UI overhauls and larger functionality updates, but time will tell.

Thank you!

Best regards,
Eric Davidson

notes.title: Qyllscape is Getting Better! V1.0.5
notes.content:
Hello!

I hope your writing is going well. Qyllscape released ~2 months ago, and I've been slowly getting back into some larger updates, and I made some big progress recently that I think will build some good momentum going forward.

Here's a list of the things that have been improved by this update, including some things that have been requested:

[list]
[*] There is now an option to toggle fullscreen mode in General Settings.
[*] There is now a "Project Details" tool that will display total words for the current project
[*] Backup folders can now be imported with the "Import Backups" tool, just drag in a folder containing .txt files and a new project will be created.
[*] A very basic first attempt at text searching has been added. It's there, but mostly as a test.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/57ae562f30ea0d85afbdd8629c462cb0b4662136.png[/img]

Things I want to work on next:

[list]
[*] Allow users to import their own backgrounds and font files.
[*] Allow users to add on-screen graphics to decorate their editors.
[*] Improve import/export to include other file formats (.epub, .docx, .pdf) 
[/list]

I still believe that Qyllscape has an immense amount of potential. I hope I'm the right person to bring that potential out of Qyllscape, and I appreciate the patience as I work on doing so. 

I also love hearing feedback, and I take it all very seriously. Hopefully given enough time, you'll start to see the things you've requested show up in Qyllscape.

Best Regards,
Eric

notes.title: Qyllscape Update #3 - Releasing Soon
notes.content:
Hello future Qyllscapers,

I'll try to keep this update brief. The short of it is, development is running smoothly, and I am finally working on some of the polishing things I've been putting off.

Keep in mind, most features are configurable, and optional, so these things can be enabled/disabled. Here's a quick list of what I've improved/added recently...

[list]
[*] Page numbers automatically update to reflect current text in project
[*] Improved mechanical keyboard sounds (random pitch, vintage variation) [Really happy here]
[*] Added test for fountain pen sounds (Needs a little tuning, but going well)
[*] Error correction within file system when detecting a corrupt project
[*] Variety of backup options (full project, condensed project, html improvements)
[*] Lighting controls are added to saved theme settings, and backed up to cloud
[*] Massively improved UI for different screen sizes, now text renders properly at higher resolutions instead of just "zooming" in
[*] Included short list of default color themes
[*] General usability updates to prevent corrupting project
[*] Successful testing of build between Windows/MacOS
[*] ...more that I can't remember!
[/list]

The point of this post is to say that I have been working on stabilizing the application and adding in polish. That process will continue after release as I work to make this as reliable of a tool as I can.

The plan is to release Qyllscape as soon as possible at this point. The hardest part is me deciding to hit the button. I am planning to take more vacation time soon from my full-time job in order to make that final push, and I want to thank everyone again for the continued support.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/0daed76ba1db383572656e6fbae589b78285df75.png[/img]

Best Regards,
Eric Davidson

notes.title: Qyllscape Update #2 - Improvements, improvements, improvements
notes.content:
Hello future Qyllscapers,

Firstly I appreciate those that have been following Qyllscape for a few months now, and wanted to share a little more about development. I am absolutely still hard at work, and I am hopeful that with a few more weeks of late nights, Qyllscape will be polished up and ready to go.

Here are a couple successes, with more details around improvement development further down...

- Cloud saving is working, so your projects should be available across machines!
- Color templates have been added, so there should be a list of prebuilt customizations for all colors (think light mode, dark mode, gorgeous mode)
- Countless improvements behind the scenes to architecture that will allow me to develop faster, and add more customization options

[h2]Foundation Rebuild[/h2]

When I start building projects, I generally piece it together as I go, and because of that, improvements are usually piled on top of each other. The issue is that as you improve something, over and over again, you learn enough to realize that what you're improving should be rebuilt from scratch.

This is difficult to do because of the Sunk-Cost fallacy, the belief that just because you have put so much effort in one approach, it should not be abandoned.

Qyllscape was pieced together as an experiment, and the foundation of that experiment needed to be replaced. The way that I have been handling the graphical resizing of various elements needed to be dealt with.

So, I basically forced myself to delete all of it, and start from scratch. This gif is crude, but represents a lot of troubleshooting, and encouraging improvements on the basic layout of the Qyllscape "book" editor. I have deleted all records of what it was like before, but it was basically a group of images carefully and manually stacked on each other, with ridiculous pixel-perfect math sprinkled throughout the code to "look" like it was doing what is happening in this gif.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/0bfe42f9af6086323334a2958cd28727ffae4863.gif[/img]

So, the new approach is smoother, promotes better performance, and is much easier to work with throughout other areas in the code.

[h2]Wave Bye To Your Darlings[/h2]

On the topic of rebuilding, I was holding on to too many aspirations for the UI. I liked the idea of having a playful, draggable UI system, but the truth I had to deal with is that it did not serve the final product, and mostly presented issue after issue related to accessibility, platform support, viewport clutter, coding complexity, etc. I adore the old, sketchy feel of the UI, but I am working to make a simple product that will help people finish their books.

The new iteration of the UI is much simpler, and will allow me to iterate even faster as I add support for more customization throughout the application.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/621edd8c0eeeaa7302d2f98b4a39c38a14c0c636.png[/img]

[h2]Getting Ready For Release[/h2]

The exciting part of these changes is that the only thing remaining before Qyllscape is available, is for me to continue testing it and polishing it up as much as possible, meaning that it is in a place now where it is usable, and someone could comfortably utilize it to write a book.

I appreciate your patience so much. My focus in the coming weeks will be around polish, and creating some advertisements for getting more people interested. If you'd like to help spread the word, check out my instagram account [url=https://www.instagram.com/ericdavidsonwrites]@ericdavidsonwrites[/url].

I can only say thank you so many times, but I am excited for what is to come. Now, back to work!

Love you all!
Eric Davidson

notes.title: Qyllscape Development Update #1
notes.content:
Dear future authors,

I am hard at work with updates to Qyllscape, and I have received such an encouraging response across platforms from people that are excited to try it out. The truth is that I made a mistake understanding release timelines, and thought I could play to the buzzer, and still get Qyllscape out on October 20th. Unfortunately, it looks like Qyllscape will not be released in October, and it is my fault.

My absolute priority is to make sure that when Qyllscape is available, it is 100% ready to support you on your writing journey. I apologize for the delay, but I think it will be worth it in the long run.

The good news is that development has been going amazingly well (albeit slowly), and some features I wasn't sure could be added are already in! 

[h2]Candlelight[/h2]

By far I think people are most excited by the concepts I introduced in the candlelight feature. Since I released the original trailer, I have overhauled the lighting system to add even more variability, with multiple lights that can be customized individually.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44362565/4a7a20fa29c685635001c93c0f959f217f60d16d.png[/img]

[h2]Exporting[/h2]

Qyllscape is not going to be industry-leading in every possible writing feature (for example exporting your work) but it is important to have basic functionality available so that people aren't forced to copy/paste their work into another software just to print it.

Now, Qyllscape has a customizable export tool that will allow basic customization before generating an HTML file, a standardized format you'll be able to open in any browser to capture the full text, or customize into PDF format for printing.

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]

I had intended for Qyllscape to be available this week, and unfortunately that won't happen. I honestly didn't expect the quick interest it would generate, and I think that interest encouraged me to put more effort into what Qyllscape can be.

I hope your writing is going well, and I look forward to delivering a satisfying and [b]complete[/b] editor for you to try out soon. I appreciate the support!

Best Regards,
Eric Davidson
